name: away_natvent_exits_at_comfort_ceiling__hvac_fan
description: [hvac_fan twin of golden 'away_natvent_exits_at_comfort_ceiling'; Issue #1193] Nat-vent while away uses free cooling until indoor reaches comfort_cool (74F), then should exit and let HVAC setback handle it. The ceiling exit while away requires Issue #231 production fix to add a comfort_cool exit gate in check_natural_vent_conditions() for away occupancy.
source: Issue #1193: hvac_fan twin of golden 'away_natvent_exits_at_comfort_ceiling' (pre-#1140 version, fan configured). The golden is locked and now asserts the no-fan 'paused' result.
notes: Production behavior (single-engine harness): nat-vent activates while home, continues after the away transition (setpoint-only change).
While away with nat-vent active, free cooling keeps indoor below setback_cool=79F.

When indoor reaches the comfort_cool=74F ceiling, the away-ceiling-exit (Issue #231, check_natural_vent_conditions Priority-2b) exits nat-vent — further open-window cooling risks dropping below comfort_heat and accumulating violations.
The nat_vent_not_active assertion captures the Issue #231 away-ceiling-exit (live in production).

hvac_fan twin (Issue #1193): with the HVAC fan configured, an open window with usable outdoor air is ventilation (fan on), not a pause. This scenario pins the ventilation/exit/setback decision only; it deliberately does NOT assert the cool setpoint that production also arms during hvac_fan ventilation (nat_vent_ac_assist_armed), which is the rule-3 question tracked in #1142.

events.note: Warm-day classification: HVAC in cool mode
Morning: indoor 72F within band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F â€” nat-vent favorable
Window opens: outdoor 65F < indoor 72F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F, outdoor < threshold 77F â€” nat-vent activates
User leaves. Production: only setpoint changes to setback_cool=79F. Nat-vent continues running.

Afternoon: indoor has risen to 74F (comfort_cool ceiling). Outdoor 68F still cooler than indoor. In production (Issue #231 fix): the AWAY_CEILING exit candidate arms via decide_nat_vent_exit() but is NOT yet sustain-confirmed (Issue #821, NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S=90s) — session still active this tick.

95s after the ceiling was first reached (> 90s NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S) — indoor still at/above comfort_cool, outdoor still cooler than indoor. AWAY_CEILING exit sustain-confirms and commits: nat-vent exits at comfort_cool ceiling to prevent further warming risk.

assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] sensor_open: outdoor 65F < indoor 72F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F, outdoor 65F <= threshold 77F â€” nat-vent activates while occupancy is home
[hvac_fan twin] Away transition: setback_cool=79F applied. This is the only change production makes on occupancy_away â€” nat-vent is not exited.

[hvac_fan twin] Issue #231 fix is live in production: when indoor reaches comfort_cool=74F ceiling while away and nat-vent is active, check_natural_vent_conditions() Priority-2b path exits nat-vent. Free cooling has done its job; further outdoor air risks over-cooling below the comfort band. Issue #821 retiming: the exit is sustain-confirmed (NAT_VENT_EXIT_SUSTAIN_S=90s) rather than committing on the instantaneous tick the ceiling was first reached — this assertion now sits 95s after that tick, on the follow-up temp_update that confirms indoor genuinely held at/above the ceiling. The nat_vent_still_active assertion at 10:00 was removed — it used the final engine snapshot (which captures the 14:01:35 exit), making it impossible to assert mid-run state. The continue-through-away behavior is covered by away_with_active_natvent_transition.

verdict.summary: [hvac_fan twin] Nat-vent uses free cooling while away, exits at comfort_cool ceiling (74F) via Issue #231 away-ceiling-exit path
verdict.observed_behavior: nat-vent activates while home, persists through away transition (setback applied), exits when indoor reaches comfort_cool=74F
verdict.expected_behavior: Free cooling opportunity exploited while away; ceiling exit at comfort_cool prevents over-cooling and accumulating comfort violations in the band
